chunks: And from him, from al-Saffan and al-Nadr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Muhrim (person in Ihram), when passing by a carcass, should not hold his nose.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.يُمْسِكْ عَلَى أَنْفِهِ: To hold the nose (a common practice to block smell)

ai.seo_question: What should a person in Ihram do when passing by a carcass?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies that a Muhrim is not required to hold his nose when passing a carcass with a mild odor, distinguishing this from cases of overwhelming stench. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle of avoiding unnecessary hardship (*raf' al-haraj*) during Hajj, ensuring that minor sensory discomforts do not invalidate the sacred state of Ihram.
